Logo Party Board Game I gave this game to my teenage nephew, who played it with several family members and friends. They found the instructions not really hard, but very long and involved, and it took awhile for them to figure out how to play the game. They tried to follow the rules, but ended up playing the game according to their own "house rules."

The game comes with a timer, which makes a very loud noise. They eventually stopped using the timer because the noise was so annoying. One player even thought that the timer might have been broken. The timer went off completely on its own, making that obnoxious noise. Another player, an adult woman, did not enjoy the game at all, but the teens enjoyed the aspect of the game that required you to draw or to describe a product or the logo or symbol for a product. The game seems to be a combination of Pictionary and Charades and Trivial Pursuit. The kids thought this was a good, creative game, with a combination of old and new products. This aspect of the game made it good for mixed age groups. As other reviewers have said, this game is best played in teams. I have the feeling that this experiment may have gone better if at least one player had really understood how to play the game so that so much time would not have been consumed in trying to understand the rules.

The teens are willing to give this game another try. I am going to edit this review after they do to see if they enjoyed the game more. I have a feeling they will, especially as they become more familiar with it.
text_fidelity_b: Logo Party Board Game

text_fidelity_a:
Never Have I Ever Parent's Edition Card Game Set | Fun Game Night Party Games for Adults | for 2+ Players | Ages 17 + i thought this would be a fun gag game. If you are in mix company (right leaning vs left leaning), I would not recommend. The basic premise of the game is that each player votes on whether they think the card is true or false, but their votes don't actually matter. The person whose turn it is reads the card out loud, makes the final decision, and follows the action on the card (whether they are right or wrong). There is an action on the card for you to perform, which usually includes drinking.

First of all, this isn't much of a game because only 1 card out of 30 is false. There is so much content from the last four years and his numerous tweets that there is enough outrageous actions for all of the cards in the game. I was hoping for some outrageous cards that were false. So, you can laugh (or cringe) about all of the things he has done, but it doesn't make it fun since there isn't much strategy. If you guess that Trump said or did the things on the card, you will be right 95% of the time.

Then, on the lower right hand corner of each card you can tell if a statement is true or false depending on whether Trump is smiling or talking. Hopefully you have good eyes because they look very similar. Also, I know it is a total gag gift, but it makes no sense that the person that actually playing is the same person that is reading the card and the answer is staring them in the face.

If you are looking for an excuse to drink while reading Trump's crazy tweets over the last 4 years, this game is for you, but I can't imagine playing this game more than once.
text_fidelity_b: Never Have I Ever Parent's Edition Card Game Set | Fun Game Night Party Games for Adults | for 2+ Players | Ages 17 +

text_fidelity_a:
Educational Insights Artie 3000 the Coding & Drawing Robot, STEM Toy, Gift for Boys & Girls, Ages 7+ The instructions in the box are lacking and the website is only slightly better. There isn't anything to download to get it to work. It works, the few times it works, via a web browser.

The device itself has a built in WiFi connection. You can, I think, secure it with a password if you want. It's open by default. You connect to it as a WiFi connection then go to its website to get it to work. I find it hangs nearly constantly. Out of the first ten tries, it worked once, each time running the same code. Here I will point out, I can't get it to go and I'm a senior software developer.

It runs on a very small surface. A sheet of 8 1/2 x 11 printer paper is perfect. It has no edge detection, so mind it doesn't wander off the edge of the table. It starts with the pen fully down by necessity, or at least I can't get it to do anything unless I fully seat the pen, which means it will touch the paper when it is set down,, so it will leave a blob that will bleed through the average paper. Indeed, these bleed almost as bad an an alcohol-based marker.

While it will work with JavaScript or Python, it provides no insight into how to use these languages, so if your kid knows Python they can learn to code the robot in Python, which just means learning its custom library. I would not go so far as to say it teaches much of anything. Hour of code shows as much, is free, and is far more reliable.

It's cute, but until the bugs are worked out, it's not worth the hassle.
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Artie 3000 the Coding & Drawing Robot, STEM Toy, Gift for Boys & Girls, Ages 7+

Friends TV Show Collage Jigsaw Puzzle 1000 Pieces Officially Licensed Friends TV Show Merchandise EDIT: initially I reviewed this before really getting into the puzzle. I’m in it now, and I can say this is one of the most poorly formulated puzzles I’ve ever done. It appears that whoever decided the pattern of the piece cut outs was lazy and decided to have repeating shapes throughout, which results in many perfect fits that are completely incorrect. In places where the differences are obvious, it’s not much of an issue, but there are also plenty of times this happens in areas that look similar, resulting in incorrect placement, backtracking, and frustration. I love puzzles, but not this one. I love friends, but I can’t stand this friends puzzle. The visual design was excellent, so whoever came up with that did a wonderful job. Lots of nostalgia, lots of little visual cues to make it fun. But whoever designed the cut out portion did an awful job.

So the puzzle itself isn’t super high res, nor are the pieces particularly inventive in how they’re cut, but man am I having fun reliving the show. Honestly, this is all about the nostalgia and having a chill time. It’s a little harder than I expected, but still totally doable. Perfect escape!

Imhotep Builder of Egypt | Family Board Game by Kosmos | 2-4 Players | Ages 10+ | Toy of The Year Finalist | Parents Choice Gold Award Winner | Toy Insider Top Holiday Toy | Spiel Des Jahres-Nominated This is just a first-time playing review, which I'll update as we continue to play. But at this point it wouldn't surprise me if the score gets bumped up to a five.

Components: high quality. They seem quite well made, durable, and are beautiful looking.

Set up: Set up is pretty easy and quick despite the number of materials (we played with three)

Gameplay: Deceptively simple. Your goal is to build structures using blocks which you quarry then place on a boat then sail to one of four places then unload them, with various points scored at the ends of rounds and the game depending on what you achieved. It is, as mentioned, deceptively simple because though you only have a few options, the other players of course get to do their own thing, which often involves blocking your thing. So that ship you were planning to load up with that particular stone you needed? Somebody just decided to sail it away. Those stone you loaded on that ship to build a pyramid? Somebody docked it instead at the obelisk area. So you need to work around what your opponents are doing, try to anticipate what they're going to do, as well as try to block them as well. It's fun, frustrating, stimulating, engaging, and did I mention fun?

We really enjoyed playing it even with the usual slow-down issues of playing a game for the first time. Even with those first game issues, the game was finished in under an hour and I would imagine you could get through it in 30 minutes regularly. An additional plus is that although the game will play differently lots of times obviously with all the variations on situations, the game itself comes with a "B" side (in other words, its own variant)

I'll update as we get more games under our hat, but right now Imhotep seems like a winner
text_fidelity_b: Imhotep Builder of Egypt | Family Board Game by Kosmos | 2-4 Players | Ages 10+ | Toy of The Year Finalist | Parents Choice Gold Award Winner | Toy Insider Top Holiday Toy | Spiel Des Jahres-Nominated

Mountains Out of Molehills | Family Board Game for 2-4 Players | Two-Level Gameboard Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Great Gateway Game for Ages 9+ This game hits that sweet spot where the complexity is enough for adults but not so high that kids struggle. And it’s FUN! It says 9 and up but my 7-year-old caught on pretty quickly and was delighted when we talked about it in terms of executing a program. My family loves this game. My husband and I can see playing it with just adults too.

The gameplay involves drafting cards and then using them to create a plan for how the mole will move on the grid, which is essentially a simple program much like one would write on a computer. It takes some strategy, but you can only predict other people so much and this is where the game shines.

I was worried it would be too complex or long when we read the rules, but it plays very smoothly! We felt comfortable within 2 rounds, and it was a lot of fun seeing how the plans we made would be thwarted as other players move. We also enjoyed how the turn order changed. There are many levels of subtle strategy, I feel like we will be learning new things each time we play. There is a random element of dice when placing a rock on the board, simple but genius game design. It keeps it from feeling unfair, and adds an element of luck to using it.

Even when you are losing, it’s so interesting to see the programs unfold as each card flips that it didn’t feel upsetting, and most of the points are earned in the later rounds as the mounds get higher so you can easily catch back up to an early lead or after a bad round. This means you don’t feel too discouraged if you have a poor start.

I like that it has a defined timeline, there are 6 rounds and you know what they will look like. Overall a great choice for a family game night as it is not likely to overrun an hour.

The double-layer boards and gameplay are unique and the story of the moles is full of flavor. The art is charming and the explanation of the rules such as “moles are too polite so they don’t move when they hit another” is a really sweet touch. The printing is great quality, the game is just beautiful to look at. The box is well-organized making setup and takedown easy, and it looks pretty on the shelf. Plus, we love the moles! The standees make great pieces. This game shows a lot of care in the details, and we love games with a lot of artistic flavor.

We play a lot of games as a family, but when we finished this one kiddo said this was their new favorite! The only downside is the limit of 2-4 players–it keeps it moving but means we can’t invite more friends to play at a time!

Bonus, the box art is beautiful so this also would make a lovely gift to open.
text_fidelity_b: Mountains Out of Molehills | Family Board Game for 2-4 Players | Two-Level Gameboard Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Great Gateway Game for Ages 9+

Cosmic Encounter 42nd Anniversary Edition Board Game - Classic Strategy Game of Intergalactic Conquest for Kids and Adults, Ages 14+, 3-5 Players, 1-2 Hour Playtime, Made by Fantasy Flight Games Ok, so every 4th of July my rather decent sized family (~30 people) gets together and has a great time. A few of us in the younger age range (<30) love to play board games and stuff like that. We had played the same games for several years and I was getting board with the same stuff. I was looking for a new challenge!

I searched for weeks, looking for a game that I thought would suffice, and I kept coming back to cosmic encounters. I finally decided to buy it. When it came in the mail I ripped everything open and started discovering the game. I was so excited and hopeful. It looked pretty complicated, ever after watching How-To's online.

I tried to get a couple of my friends to play it, but after watching me setup the game (still barely having a clue how to play) they gave up and wanted to play 3's (a simple card game).

So there my expensive new game sat for weeks... months... a year! I finally got one of my cousins to play it with me, but we had to switch off playing a third person. We hardly had a clue how to play, but it sparked his interest.

The few times we got together after that, we just didn't get the time to play the game but his interest stayed.

Finally, a friend of mine and I went up to my cabin, and my cousin happened to be there.

I had brought the game, so we decided to finally play it the with the right number of players! After each of us read through the manual, we started playing. There was a fair amount of confusion with the rules, and how the game actually played out, but we managed to finish the game. We then played another, and another after that. The game was a blast! We discovered a new rule or something we hadn't been doing right practically every game. We actually played 3 or 4 whole games before we learned we were supposed to be able to get 2 encounters per turn!

Every game we played we got more and more accustomed to the game, and we enjoyed it a little more. I now cant wait to play it again, and I am getting more people involved with it. I am planning on buying the expansions as well!

Long story short, it is a somewhat difficult game to learn, but once you do it is a blast! Each game took about 30 minutes to an hour with three people.

I definitely recommend it if your looking for a good board game!
text_fidelity_b: Cosmic Encounter 42nd Anniversary Edition Board Game - Classic Strategy Game of Intergalactic Conquest for Kids and Adults, Ages 14+, 3-5 Players, 1-2 Hour Playtime, Made by Fantasy Flight Games

Putting the chickens in the nest, collecting the eggs into the bucket, moving Barbie around and having conversations with the chickens, making the chickens say peep peep peep!

As for the set, my only suggestion would be to make the eggs able to come out of the a container. Even if this means that most of the eggs immediately got lost, it would provide so much more opportunity for fun and creativity. In order to allow my daughter to collect eggs into the bucket, I made a few eggs out of oven baked clay so that she would have a little bit more opportunity for interactive play.

My complaints about this Barbie doll are my usual complaints, I wish that this Barbie was shaped a little bit more like Daisy, and I wish that this Barbie moved a little bit more like the sports Barbies. I wish that all Barbies off the shelf would come with more functional joints so that Barbie could do more interesting things. However! My three-year-old has noticed no lack, and I think the fact that Barbie is rather inflexible makes her somewhat easier to get dressed, which is fun. This Barbie has a very sweet, engaging face, and even though this toys for children, I'll be honest and say that I genuinely enjoy playing with this set with my daughter.

Matchbox Cars, Large-Scale, 15-in Toy Recycling Truck with Garbage Bin, Lights and Sounds This recycling truck is awesome. It takes two AA batteries (included for demonstration purposes only—meaning they may have to be replaced using a Phillips screwdriver shortly after use). The biggest difficulty I had is in removing this truck from the box because it arrives in the ON condition and started working immediately as I was trying to unpack it. That was a bit annoying.

The on / off button is located underneath the truck under the cab. There are two levels of sound and lights to choose from when turning on.

Once the truck is on, the button in the center of the CAB turns on the ignition sounds and the lights come on.

The lights also come on when pressing down on the tires and moving forward and backward. When moving backward, the backup warning sounds activate.

The recycling truck container opens in back and can store Legos or other small toys. It also tilts back to the rear.

All the sounds of dumping, loading, and idling are realistic. Pressing down on the horns on either side of the cab also generates realistic sounds.

The recycling bucket has a slot that allows for placement into the hitch. Once in place, move the lever handle down to dump (or pretend dump) what is in the pail. The pail can also be stored in the top of the truck’s container.

The instructions are useless as it only talks about the batteries. Therefore, it is important to pay attention to the pictures on the box or read the description on Amazon to learn how to fully operate this vehicle. Another option is to learn via trial and error.

To me this is an extremely impressive toy for a reasonable price of $29.99.
text_fidelity_b: Matchbox Cars, Large-Scale, 15-in Toy Recycling Truck with Garbage Bin, Lights and Sounds

Moose Racing Mission: Diamond Heist Game Board with Spy, Challenges and Instructions, Multi (91009) This is a really cool and interesting game! I wasn't sure what to expect based on the box and description, but unlike other contraption based games I've played (like the classic "mouse trap" from my youth), this is more of a cooperative play game.
There are 4 strings that move a (clearly mission-impossible inspired) suspended character around the playing board, and it takes careful pulling and releasing each of them as a group effort to navigate properly, sort of like a marionette puppet meets a corporate team building activity. There are some things to do like remove security cameras and traps but the truth is, the real fun doesn't start until you open up the jewel cage.
Once the cage is open, there's a countdown (you can hear the spring noise whirring as soon as it opens) and the police car starts to slowly circle the board. If you make it to the getaway car with the jewel before the car makes it to block your path, you win! If, however, you take too long, the police car will spring into place and block your path. Hilarity ensues as players start to panic and lose their cool, and in the end, whether you make it or not, it felt exciting.
Things I like about the game:
- It is cooperative, not individual. So you don't "beat" another player, you work as a team to complete the task in time.
- The mechanical game board is unique and really fun to learn
- It does NOT require batteries! The board uses spring loaded timers where necessary, no electricity. This is cool in a decidedly analog way.
- People can walk over and see how it is played and join with very little instruction

Things I did not, however, like:
- The truth is, when playing with my kids, we sort of skipped the first part of the game and just jumped to the jewel part. The designers of this game tried to make it longer by adding disarming traps and pulling security cameras in particular order based on cards, but it felt tedious after a few rounds. Really the fun part is the end. The whirring police car gives a sense of danger and urgency that makes it fun.
- That little spy is suspended by strings that get tangled so quickly and easily. It feels like I sneeze and they are tangled. Out of the box, I had to spend time untwisting it before we played for the first time, so be careful.

That being said, the game is TON of fun for different ages and we actually had some guests come over who looked at it and wanted to play too (adults AND kids). They all asked where to to get it, so it might become a regular thing found in our neighborhood. I'd say it deserves 5 stars, it's been a while since a game sparked this much interest that wasn't on a screen.
text_fidelity_b: Moose Racing Mission: Diamond Heist Game Board with Spy, Challenges and Instructions, Multi (91009)

Crayola Super Tips Washable Markers Age 3+ - 50 Count I'll admit it: I'm an adult who loves to color. I find it a great way to relax, and there are some amazing "coloring books for adults" gaining popularity these days (Johanna Basford, Angie Grace, etc.). And there are whole communities of "colorists" popping up on social media.

So naturally, I'm looking for different mediums to use when I color. I've used colored pencils and gel pens, so I figured it was time to branch out into the marker arena. Someone suggested starting with these as they're water-based rather than alcohol-based, and Amazon has them at a good price, so I got the 50-ct set.

Overall, I'm pleased. There is a good selection of colors, several shades of each, which helps to bring some variety into th mix.

What I DON'T like (and this seems to be a problem for ALL coloring mediums): the actual color of the pen/pencil/etc. almost NEVER matches the color of the cap/barrel/etc. I realize that colors will look different depending on the type a "color" of paper used as the background, but seriously, some of these are WAY off. I find myself having to make a "cheat sheet" on the paper I'm using just so I can get a clear picture of how the various colors REALLY look.

Like I said, this isn't just a problem with Crayola, but they make it a little more difficult because the pens have NO distinguishing markings on them whatsoever to designate a color number or code. I ended up putting little pieces of masking tape on each pen and numbering them myself just so I can keep the color charts coordinated.

All that aside, they work great once you figure out the colors. Colors are vibrant, and I had very little "bleed through" or feathering in an Angie Grace book. Bleed through and feathering depend a great deal on the paper used, so bear that in mind and ALWAYS test before coloring.

Overall​, I like these - don't "love" them, but they're good quality water-based markers at a very good price.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola Super Tips Washable Markers Age 3+ - 50 Count

text_fidelity_a:
Imagine Meditation Kit for Kids - Award-Winning Mindfulness kit of XL Cards with Calming Guided Meditations for Empowerment, Focus and Relaxation. Great for Parents, Teachers and Therapists. This kit was made to help families like ours. I am a stay at home mom to four kids (11yo and younger). Prior, I was an artist and earned a Special Ed and a Rehabilitation degree. My background has been useful because we ended up a household full of ADHD, severe anxiety, learning and speech disabilities, plus more. We have been using this set for three weeks now and it has proven invaluable. It truly was an excellent find.

We do not own the original set (with the Dove on the box), but I suspect this new version is probably an upgraded improvement of the first box set. It looks very similar, except now there appears have some new (maybe better) ideas and slightly more guidance in this new version. I don't mean to imply this set is a duplicate of the first set, nor am I trying to discourage you from buying both. I simply don't know. I came to the conclusion that these were similar after reading the reviews for the first one. Had I been given the option to chose between the two sets, I would have chosen to start with the newer set I am reviewing here today. Simply because of the changes that were made.

ABOUT THE PRODUCT:

- Most of the cards appear to have between 200 to 300 words. Each activity lasts about 5 minutes per card, give or take. Of course each could be longer or shorter because you get decide how much time you want to spend.

- This newer set has a total of 24 meditation activity cards. 18 of the 24 are guided scenarios. The 18 cards are "story like, short guided imaginary meditation with different scenes that people can imagine themselves taking a part of.” Meaning they ask you to concentrate and imagine yourself in a particular story line (like "walking through the woods" or "stargazing on a warm summer night", for example).
- 6 of those 18 cards mentioned above focus on our senses (touch, taste, etc).
- In addition to the above 18, there are 6 more "positive affirmation" cards. These affirmations address different times of day (morning or bedtime) -or- feelings (anger, stress, etc).

OTHER COMPARISON NOTES:
- From what I can tell, the original set only appears to have 23 guided imaginary "walk through the woods" type scenarios. It does not specifically explore common human experiences that center around feeling or our body.
- The Legend Card is unique to this set. The Legend is more of a guide chart that will help you quickly find the most useful card, depending on the your feelings/needs at the moment­.
- Both sets have the same breathing exercise card.

MY POSITIVES:

- This set is excellent quality. The cards are very nice and are made of a thick paperboard. They are technically laminated, though it wouldn't consider it a plastic waterproof type of covering. It feels more like a wax coating that is water resistant. But it is a sturdy material.
-This truly is an activity for all ages. Kids 6 and younger will probably need guidance. Around 6 or 7, this could probably be an independent activity for most kids. But this mediation set is NOT just for kids. I think pre-teens, teens, and even adults can still benefit from these cards. I wish I made more time to use them myself, tbh.
- These have been excellent in helping everyone in our house decompress and cope with our daily stressors.
- I think this encourages and even teaches how to use our imaginations better (an essential skill!!!).
- It has increases our awareness of self worth. And in a sense, these also teach us to take responsibility for some of our thoughts and feelings too. These activities seem to encourage future motivation and action too.
-This kit is secular and inclusive. Meaning it is not religions in any way. And Many people are represented in the images. The language the cards use, and the activities are age and gender neutral. The suggested scenarios are something anyone can envision.
- And the art is beautiful.

THE NEGATIVES:
- The box is terrible. It's too small. It's impossible to find the one card the Ledged Guide tells you to grab without taking out the entire stack. And it's a pain putting the cards away. I'm going to have to come up with a better storage system.
- There are spelling mistakes, improper punctuation, and unnecessary capitalization. If it had been here or there, I wouldn't have said anything. Nor am I in a position to judge. But it's really bad and does not feel educational.
- The price feels a bit steep initially. However, I think if you make it a goal to give this set a real try and use it for a little while, I think you'll see the $30 price tag actually feels like a good deal.

The cars eerily control themselves around the huge 4 foot by 8 foot track. The were mesmerized while controlling the cars in and out of lanes. They really do work like slot cars, but with a wide open track.

However, after racing for a little while, my kids started getting frustrated that the cars would occasionally go into a spin and shoot off the track or end up heading the wrong direction, which they would quickly notice and reverse, but it was frustrating when your car would spin and start going the wrong way. Often you would see a car fly off the track and be told to return the car to the track. It happens enough to be intrusive to the game.

The battling aspect of the game is great. The cars do seem to have a sense of aim when firing. But we did run into a little trouble. My older son ended up playing with his car for an hour, building up points and adding upgrades to his car. Now his car is heads and shoulders above my youngest's and there is frustration for my youngest since they are no longer competing on par.

We are still in awe of the technology and we still enjoy playing with it, but it is a little short of perfect.

BlueFit German Tiger I Panzer Tank with Remote Control, Battery, Light, Sound, Rotating Turret and Recoil Action When Cannon Artillery Shoots, Mini 1:72 Scale, Assorted Color This this is awesome. For something that easily sits on the palm of your hand the detail is pretty sharp. It honestly looks like a World War ][ Tiger tank with tons of details. I received the standard, mostly green, camouflage there's also a darker camouflage and a blue tank available. Colors appear to ship randomly. Remote control device coloring also seem to match the tank you get.
This little thing really zips around. I was surprised at how quick it gets up and goes. There's also a super speed button on the controller that adds fifty percent to the speed of the tank. There's also engine noises and what I'm guessing are 'track' sounds are this races around. The turret will turn 360° in one direction, I found going one way the barrel would hang up on the antenna but the turret rotation switches back and forth as you rotate. The barrel also raises and lowers as the turret turns. When you press the fire button there's the sound of a cannon firing and the entire tank body recoils backwards.
The remote control takes four double A batteries and the tank itself charges from a cable attached to the side of the remote. Charging time is fairly quick and I've already gotten several hours of fun out of the tank and it's still going strong. The only reason I can't give it four stars is the tank just won't drive in a straight line. You can someone adjust for the tendency to turn by steering left or right as you go but it would have been just that much cooler if it had driven in a straight line. Still, I'm a fully grown adult and this is one of my favorite things. It's just such a gas to play with.
I received this item in exchange for my review.

LEGO City Police Station 60246 Police Toy, Fun Building Set for Kids (743 Pieces) I can’t help but mentally compare the 2020 version of the Lego City Police Station to the 2017 version of the Lego City Police Station. And when I do that, the older version looks far better to my eye than the new one does.

I usually look at sets from an AFOL’s (adult fan of Lego) perspective, which is admittedly different than a kid’s. I usually want my sets to look cool on display and/or have a fun building experience. Lego building is great fun and stress relief even when you’re an adult.

Anyway, I think this set looks like it was released during my childhood, twenty years ago. It’s bland and basic, a bunch of rectangles plopped on top of each other. Even the police car and search truck look like boxes on wheels.

That said, there are a few things I like about the set. I like the drone, the exploding cell, the searchlight, and the table tennis (though I was disappointed the table uses stickers). I can see how there’s a lot for younger builders to play with, especially given the variety of minifigures and areas in the police station.

K’NEX Revolution Ferris Wheel Building Set – 344 Pieces with Battery Powered Motor – Ages 7+ Engineering Education Toy [[VIDEOID:5795137e2a23bd3d76a56d2b9446c889]] If you’re already familiar with K’Nex building sets, this K’NEX THRILL RIDES-REVOLUTION FERRIS WHEEL is a simple, fast build. The Ferris wheel is big, but it doesn’t require a lot of pieces. Also, much of the assembly involves building duplicate parts that combine to make the wheel and its swinging gondolas.

The set is recommended for age 7+, and that sounds reasonable (assuming that an adult provides some initial help with making the connections, and assists with lifting the wheel onto the axle). Each shape of piece is a different color, which detracts from the appearance of the finished Ferris wheel, but makes the construction simpler. There aren’t many “snowflake” connections, which I usually have to puzzle over to get the right orientation. (K’Nex pieces are much harder to work with than LEGO pieces.) The instructions are reasonably clear. This set took me about 5 hours to build (from opening the box to completion, working at a leisurely pace).

Unfortunately, the finished “thrill ride” isn’t very thrilling. Like a full-sized amusement park ride, the Ferris wheel doesn’t do much—it just goes around and around in a circle. Also, it does NOT have a variable speed control—you cannot start, stop, or speed up the wheel gradually (like a real ride). Although the motor has a single speed, it does run in forward and reverse directions. The motor is powered by two AA batteries (not included).

For the Ferris wheel to turn properly, one edge of the inner wheel track must be settled into the groove on the “gear wheel” attached to the motor. You can easily fiddle with the base to adjust things so that the track and groove always make good contact. Because it’s sort of boring and lacks a variable speed control, I rate this K’Nex Ferris Wheel kit at 4 stars (“I like it” on the official Amazon scale).
text_fidelity_b: K’NEX Revolution Ferris Wheel Building Set – 344 Pieces with Battery Powered Motor – Ages 7+ Engineering Education Toy

text_fidelity_a:
Wonder Forge Richard Scarry's Busytown, Eye Found It Toddler Toy and Game (5 players) for Boys and Girls Age 3 and Up - A Fun Preschool Board Game,Multi-colored Excellent game for toddlers and preschoolers! This collaborative game (everyone works as a team) is so easy to learn and play. For two to four players, the game board is three piece, six foot long puzzle. After you set up the board, everyone has a marker. There are about ten magnifying glasses, a cardboard boat, six cardboard pieces of food, cards, a spinner, and a timer. The goal? Everyone has to make it to the boat and the boat has to make it to Picnic Island before the pigs eat all the food. The youngest person goes first.

Each player spins the spinner. The arrow lands on either a Move, a Bug, or a Pig. If you spin to a Move, you move your marker that many spaces and the next player goes. If you spin to a Pig, the Pigs "eat" one picnic food item and you take one food items away and spin again. If you spin to a bug, you pull a card. When you pull the card, you have to look throughout the game board for those items (almost Where's Waldo style). For example, if you pull a card with pictures of "balloons", you set the timer and look all around the game board for balloons. You use the magnifying glasses to mark that you've found one. When the timer is up you count how many "balloons" you found and all players move that many spaces. So if you found three balloons, everyone moves three spaces. Once everyone lands on the boat, everyone takes turns to spin to move the boat to Picnic Island. So long as the pigs haven't eaten all the food, everyone wins!

This game is a great concept for kids who have issues with winning and losing. Especially at 3 and 4 years of age when other skills like patience, taking turns, and working together are my main focus for my son rather than learning to be a gracious loser (I hope to teach him this later). Focusing and patience are the skills that this game builds as my son loves being a helper and the idea that he is helping for everyone to win actually helps him to focus and be a little more patient. The game also helps with counting and memory. I am pleasantly surprised by this game and I highly recommend it!
text_fidelity_b: Wonder Forge Richard Scarry's Busytown, Eye Found It Toddler Toy and Game (5 players) for Boys and Girls Age 3 and Up - A Fun Preschool Board Game,Multi-colored

The brush has real hair bristles and is medium sized, which is good for administering a base coat, but not so great for detail work. The rocks photographed for this kit clearly are made with the help of paint pens or fine detail brushes. What is most valuable in this kit is the book.
The book has a lot of valuable information for painting in general and for rocks in particular. Some things might seem obvious to an adult but not so obvious to a child, such as, "To make a pastel, mix a tiny bit of color into a blob of white." The advice to let paint dry between colors is repeated several times, and in my experience, kids need to hear that more than once! There are tons of cool ideas for painting. Flowers, food, pirates, animals, names, and more are featured.
This klutz kit is a good starting point for young rock painters. I would present it as a gift along with some fine point brushes or fine point paint pens, smooth rocks, and perhaps a few Apple Barrel acrylics.

Disney Princess Fashion Doll Castle, Dollhouse 3.5 feet Tall with 16 Accessories and 6 Pieces of Furniture (Amazon Exclusive) This took us about an hour to put together, and was rather frustrating to assemble. That said, I hate assembling toys like this where when you snap them into place, they are almost impossible to un-snap, so you've gotta be really 100% sure before you put things together. However, once it was built – this thing is pretty epic! My kids had an absolute blast playing with it and really loved all of the Royal, golden elements.

My only issue is that I was never able to get the swing to actually function, I think I'm probably need to use some twist ties or my glue gun to make it stay put. It will swing, but as soon as you put dolls on it, the bottom wants to fall off of the swing holders. My husband couldn't figure it out either, and neither could my eight-year-old, who is remarkably good at assembling toys.

Other than that, this has just about anything one could want in a beautiful Royal Castle, lots of exciting and elegant items, areas to conduct creative play, etc.

Two critical pieces of feedback:

First, the backside has a sticking out part right in front of the door that probably helps the castle not fall over backwards, but has the side effect of making it so that you can't push this up against the wall, which is kind of unfortunate for places with limited space.

Second, I've noticed that my kids love dollhouses and items that have a little bit more of an interactive elements such as a slide, zip line, etc. I think the nonfunctional swing was meant to do the trick, but I think if they had added a few more interactive things, this would have a little bit more appeal for kids as they get older also.
text_fidelity_b: Disney Princess Fashion Doll Castle, Dollhouse 3.5 feet Tall with 16 Accessories and 6 Pieces of Furniture (Amazon Exclusive)

SmartLab Toys It's Alive Slime Lab SmartLab Toys It’s Alive Slime Lab is just one of dozens and dozens of slime toys intended to fascinate the young scientist in your home. The way most of these labs works is similar: Combine the included slime mix, if any exists, with a few household items like baking soda, vinegar, cornstarch, etc., and let the fun begin.

This slime toy works like the others in terms of the mixing, but it is also different than others, and I mean that in a good way. With this slime lab, the mixture is placed atop a motor that vibrates for greater effect. Kids can watch the colors and textures swirl around as the vibrations create some fun and very visual patterns. The instructions include 20 different recipes for slime and each can be made using items found in most kitchens.

What I probably like best about this slime lab is the lack of mess! Okay, there is some mess but in relative terms, the messiness is kept under control very well. The key difference is that, with most other slime labs my kids have used, messiness is encouraged. These other labs involve sticking hands in the slime, spreading it with your hands, and so on. This is messy and gross, and if multiple kids are involved, they often end up smearing it on each other, splattering it on the floors and more. There is no problem like that with SmartLab. The slime, for the most part, stays in the bowl, out of your way.

Educational toys are nice and SmartLab Toys It’s Alive Slime Lab is a toy that does get kids thinking and asking questions. My girls like it and have returned to it more than once, creating more slime and learning about household chemicals and how they react. It’s a good choice of toy that will keep kids entertained as they learn.
text_fidelity_b: SmartLab Toys It's Alive Slime Lab

Ontel Magic Tracks Police Chase Glow in The Dark Racetrack Set with 10 Feet of Speedway OK, first off - we really love Magic/Neo/Twister Tracks. We have a number of different sets. Recently we grabbed the one with the single car and remote, along with the Rocket Racers and an off brand, dinosaur-themed set. All of which were excellent! This however, has a major flaw.

The jump ramp seems like an afterthought. It looks nothing like the picture on the box. It's like the box graphics were designed before the physical product. Even worse, its the connection to the track makes zero sense, and the instructions are laughable to say the lease. Oddly enough, the ramp is able to move back and forth like a see-saw, yet, it's not meant to do that! It's a ramp - and it's supposed to let the truck fly off and onto the lower track. Here's the kicker: one side of the ramp is blocked, like a dead end, so the only way we got this to work was to lay the proceeding track over it so it the truck wouldn't be stopped. It's like the manufacture designed this ramp piece wrong. Between that, and the see saw spring built in, my bet is, this was meant to originally do something else, but it failed, so they left it that way and simply called it a jump ramp. At 29.95, that's a disgrace. This is the only set we sent back. Most of the high ratings you see are for the other themes (firetruck, police set, etc..), so proceed with caution.

T.S. Shure Map of the World Magnetic Playboard and Puzzle Well, this was kind of educational, and it was kind of a frenetic, fun 15 minutes trying to put things back together, but the end comments were "This is ridiculous" and "Well they could have made that better." The ridiculous part was how they made decisions to cut the pieces. They do not follow international borders very faithfully and randomly cut larger countries into random parts. Pieces that include only one country do not resemble the country at all. the eastern united states is a irregular rectangle that appears to miss New England and average out Florida. France is a strange amporphous shape. Canada and Russia are random blotches of non interconnecting shapes.

I like the story that the first puzzle was a US map cut into pieces in a classroom to teach geography. This could have been similar except that the countries are so crudely hacked in shapes. But it does give an idea of location and cultural icons like the great wall of china, russian dolls, local animals are located on the map. I was very impressed that the Great Barrier Reef made the map as an entity. But it could have been so much better in the way it was handled.

As for how it was made, the pieces are small and found to be easy to misplace. The magnetism is weak but sufficient to keep the pieces loosely on the board. The backing is very flexible and all in all it does not seem to be a super well built product.

Hot Wheels Track Builder Build Your Race Playset Out of all the newer 2016 Track Builder Releases, this in my opinion, is the best! There are multiple ways of setting up various layouts which the manual suggests, and good variety of pieces, though straight track are lacking as usual. The star of this show is no doubt, the duel booster! It's very "next gen-ish", as it looks nothing like boosters that have been around forever. What makes it unique is the way it is set up. There's your usual battery-eating power brick (this uses 4 D cells), but both boosters are independent from the power source. They simply plug in to the battery block, so you can place them away from each other, giving your layout twice the power to shoot your cars around. You don't have to use both boosters, but why wouldn't you? What's more interesting is, the booster's rollers are now vertical, instead of horizontal. When a HW car enters, a single rubber roller grips it from above and launches it out, and both boosters pack a punch! I only wish the connecting cords could have been longer, as you can't place the boosters too far way from each other.

The white support towers are one of the newer pieces found in this series, as they can be placed horizontally or vertically to support tracks. Each tower offers a number of node connections, so tracks can be connected at various heights using the pivot points. The pivot points are brilliant little button-like gizmos that slide easily slide into any track. Now when you snap your track into any of the towers, you can actually rotate and angle your track with much freedom. All in all, it's a very roller coaster-style approach to track building, and a good one at that.

As far as the layouts go, there are a few duel shoot outs as in...gravity drop to booster, through loop, then off to space (hopefully, a carpeted one). These are short lived, 2 second runs but kids will have fun launching their cars simultaneously (this set only comes with one car of course). One interest layout features a continuous run where both boosters work together to continuously shoot your cars through a figure 8 course. Cars zoom around and eventually crash, so it becomes a survivor game. The sample courses won't hold a child's attention for long periods, but they can experiment on their own, and combine the pieces with other sets.

And finally, the box. The new, thicker cardboard box also doubles up as an extra stunt accessory. Perforated cut outs allow tracks to be integrated for even more variety. If your kid rather keep the box, then get ready for a shock: You can actually fit all the pieces back in the box for storage. I know, right?

Overall, this is example of Mattel heading in the right direction.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Track Builder Build Your Race Playset

ADORA Baby Doll Stroller with Color Changing Sunny Days Print, Fits Up to 18 Inch Baby Dolls 3 stars

This stroller is very cute, and it is nice that it is in gender-neutral colors, so that boy children as well as girl children can enjoy this stroller. It can be used not just to hold baby dolls, but also stuffed animals.

This toy stroller resembles a typical human-baby, umbrella stroller in design and functionality. The difference between this and a real stroller, though, other than the miniature sizing, is that it is not sturdy. Therefore, there is a safety element in that your child may easily push or lean harder on its handles than it is built to withstand, and end up tripping and falling on top of or tumbling headfirst over it. If you have stairs in your house, this in particular could lead to a dangerous injury.

A major factor contributing to this flimsiness issue is the fact that the wheels are not at all strong and, overall, this toy is very cheaply made. It is certainly not constructed to stand up to the rather rugged treatment a toddler or preschooler would give to a toy like this.

In short, this doll stroller is certainly not a case of, "You get what you pay for." Because of the expensive price of this and all other Adora doll accessories, you'd think you'd be getting something really sturdy and long-lasting. Unfortunately, that is not the case with this stroller.
